title: Sam Altman's career advice: work on what's important, move fast, compound over the long run
summary: A list of career principles from Sam Altman after running Y Combinator. He stresses picking important work, scaling more than you expect, using power laws and compounding, moving fast, and executing with determination. It also covers team, meeting and goal-setting habits.

principles.text: Keep working on the most important thing you can, even when others don't get it; important is not popular.
principles.quote: However, they are willing to work on something for a long time even if other people don't get it. "Important" does not mean "popular."

principles.text: Optimize for being spectacularly right sometimes and cheaply wrong often.
principles.quote: Optimize for being spectacularly right some of the time, and low-stakes wrong a lot of the time.

principles.text: You can scale almost anything more than you think, with bigger payoffs than expected.
principles.quote: You can almost always scale things up more than you think, and the benefits to doing so are almost always bigger and more surprising than you think.

principles.text: Scale benefits, network effects and power laws are underrated and make competing against you hard.
principles.quote: Scale benefits, network effects, and the power law are so powerful that people usually delude themselves into thinking otherwise. They are often the best way to make it hard for others to compete with you.

principles.text: The key to success is making things happen: determination, execution focus and not quitting at roadblocks.
principles.quote: If there is a single key to success, it is the trait of being able to make things happen in the world

principles.text: Compounding success, meaning growth for an early-stage startup, solves almost all internal problems, especially hard ones.
principles.quote: Compounding success (which means "growth" in the case of an early-stage start-up) solves almost all internal problems, particularly hard ones.
